set.body:
Source: docs/plans/2026-07-26-evidence-coherence-representation.md, the approved follow-up to the 2026-07-25 full-codebase review whose eleven correctness findings shipped as P6f.28-P6f.39.

Objective:
Close the five structural gaps that remained once everything findable by reading had been fixed: unvalidated Slurm CLI contracts, O(n^2) journal event reads, three parallel JSON encodings of the same domain types, a binary-compatibility gate that checks nothing, and a boxed byte representation that costs ~5x memory and makes frame decoding quadratic.

Sequence (the ordering is the substance of this epic):
  P6f.18 (4a) -> P7.1 (evidence, parallel) -> P6f.10 -> P7.3 -> P7.2 -> P6f.23 -> P6f.12 -> P7.6

Three non-obvious constraints drove that order:
- The representation swap (P7.2) must precede owning the codecs (P6f.12), or every public codec is hand-written twice.
- The swap is only safe now: P6f.30 golden fixtures plus the envelope/invocation/log-page/timing/state fixtures are the detector for a silent wire change, and they did not exist before 2026-07-25.
- P6f.18 splits. Its infrastructure half goes first; cutting the 0.1.0 baseline must go last, because P7.2 changes Vector[Byte] in public signatures across nine modules and would burn a baseline published before it.

Completion rule:
This epic remains open until every phase closes with verification held to the P6f.28-P6f.39 standard: the test must fail against the pre-fix code before it counts. Real-site acceptance on an authenticated cluster stays P6f.5a and P5.

Explicitly out of scope: the Site layer, SSH protocol multiplexing (ADR 0003 one-process-per-request stands).
set.title: EPIC P7: Evidence, coherence, and byte representation
